item.title: Key Account Manager
item.description:
🌍 A Bit About Us

We’re Doccla, and we’re redefining where and how healthcare is delivered.

Our Virtual Ward and Remote Monitoring Solutions enable hospitals and health systems to care for patients at home. We support patients across the full care journey from early discharge and acute recovery to long-term condition management and proactive care.

We provide everything clinicians need to deliver safe, effective Virtual Care: medical-grade devices, logistics, patient onboarding, EHR integration, and an end-to-end clinical platform built around real-world workflows.

We currently work with over 60% of NHS ICBs and supporting health systems across the including UK, Ireland, France, and the DACH region to reduce hospital pressure, improve outcomes, and create a more resilient model of care.

We’re backed by top European investors, having secured £35m in Series B funding led by Lakestar, with participation from Elaia, General Catalyst, Speedinvest, and Bertelsmann.

🚀 Why Join Us?

This is your chance to join Doccla at a key stage in our growth.

We’re building the category leader in Virtual Care and Remote Patient Monitoring. You’ll be part of a highly entrepreneurial, mission-driven team that combines expertise across clinical, technical, commercial, and operational domains.

We’re solving real problems for patients and health systems and growing fast.

🧑‍⚕️ What You’ll Do as a Key Account Manager

You own a portfolio of HSE & NHS accounts end to end. You are the single point of accountability for everything that happens on your accounts, and you are measured above all on two things: how happy your clients are, and how much your accounts grow.

Growth here means deepening the relationships you already have. You grow the number of patients on existing pathways, add new clinical pathways, and lead clients through virtual ward delivery and into proactive, population-level care. You build trust at every level of the client, from the ward nurses using our platform every day to the senior executives who sign the contracts. Delivery excellence and genuinely happy clients are the foundation that makes all of this possible.

✅ What Experience You’ll Bring to the Team

Own your accounts end to end

  • Act as the named owner and single point of accountability for a portfolio of NHS & HSE accounts

  • Keep your clients as happy as possible, and treat their satisfaction as the foundation of everything, because happy clients renew, grow and advocate

  • Own the account plan, the renewals and the relationship from end to end, supported by your Key Accounts Lead and Operations team.

  • Be the voice of your clients inside Doccla, and their point of escalation when they need one

Grow your accounts

  • Grow the number of patients on existing pathways, so every account reaches its full potential

  • Add new clinical pathways to accounts that are ready for them

  • Identify and lead expansion from virtual ward delivery into proactive, community-based care for the highest-risk populations

  • Use the client's own data to size each opportunity and build the business case, working with the commercial and clinical teams

  • Carry and deliver against a retention and growth target, and lead renewals early to secure contracts on strong terms

Build relationships at every level

  • Build trusted relationships across the whole client, from ward nurses and clinical leads, through operational and senior executives.

  • Become genuinely embedded in how your clients work, so you spot opportunities and risks before anyone else does

  • Lead client meetings independently: steering groups, Quarterly Business Reviews and executive reviews, with support of the Partnership Managers.

  • Turn satisfied clients into advocates, case studies and references

Oversee delivery and implementation

  • Oversee delivery across your accounts and the implementation of new clients and new pathways, coordinating Product, Clinical, Patient Support and Logistics to hit go-live dates

  • Own the project plan and stakeholder map for every account

  • Own SLA and outcome reporting, and use it to build action plans and evidence value

  • Drive product adoption and utilisation, so every client uses what they are paying for

💡 What We’re Looking For

  • 2 to 4 years in account management, customer success, delivery or a client-facing role, with a track record of keeping clients happy and growing the accounts you own

  • A commercial mindset. You are comfortable owning renewals and growth, carrying a number, and spotting upsell inside an existing relationship, whether that is more patients, new pathways or new services

  • A natural relationship-builder who is equally credible with a ward nurse and a senior executive, and who enjoys becoming embedded in how a client works

  • A consultative, Challenger-style approach: you can reframe a client's thinking, build a business case and hold a commercial conversation with senior stakeholders

  • Experience in a tech, SaaS or startup environment (essential). You've worked somewhere fast-moving where the rulebook didn't always cover the situation

  • Experience in the NHS, HSE Ireland, health tech or another regulated environment (strongly advantageous)

  • Confidence leading meetings independently with senior clinical, operational and finance stakeholders

  • Strong organisation. You keep multiple accounts and implementations running without losing track of any of them

  • Comfort with CRM and reporting tools: HubSpot, Jira, Looker and Lightdash

  • A proactive, problem-solving mindset. You work across Product, Engineering, Clinical and Commercial to get the right outcome. You don't passively escalate and you don't get stuck waiting

You'll thrive here if you

  • Put client happiness first and understand that it is what unlocks renewals and growth

  • Are commercially driven and take ownership of your numbers, not just your tasks

  • Are reliable. Clients and colleagues know they can count on you to follow through without being chased

  • Adopt AI and new tools proactively to make yourself and your team faster. You don't wait for permission to try something useful

  • Spot problems in how we work and bring solutions, not just complaints. You'll often improve a process before anyone asks you to

  • Care about making an impact on how healthcare is delivered, whether that's a nurse monitoring a patient or a patient at home using our device for the first time

🧠 How We Work

We empower everyone at Doccla to take ownership of their work and the company's mission. We act ethically and always put patient safety and outcomes first.

To thrive here, you’ll need a can-do attitude and an action-oriented approach, along with a willingness to learn and grow through open feedback.

We’re a hybrid team, with offices in London, Denmark, Germany. Most of our team is London-based and enjoys in-person time at our WeWork HQ 1–3 days per week, where you’ll find great lunch, barista coffee, and a pet-friendly space. Some of our teams are fully remote, depending on the team and responsibilities. This includes our Engineering, Clinical & Patient Support teams.

🎁 What You’ll Get

Annual Leave & Holidays
🌴 25 days annual leave + up to 8 UK bank holidays [this varies depending on the role]
🔄 Option to buy or sell holidays

Remote Working
🏡 Flexible remote options
💻 Remote working stipend

Financial Benefits
📈 Employee stock options
💸 4% pension on full basic pay
🛡️ 4x salary life insurance

Health & Wellness
🩺 Private health insurance
🫄 4 months full pay for birthing parent*
👶🏽 4 weeks full pay for non-birthing parent*
👶🏽 Phased return back to paid work
🤒 Sick pay

In-Office Perks (London HQ)
🍝 Free daily lunch
🐶 Pet-friendly office

Other Benefits
📚 £500 L&D budget per person
🚲 Cycle to work scheme

Via Smart Health:
🧑‍⚕️ 24/7 GP appointments
🧠 Mental health support
🥗 Nutrition & fitness advice
🧪 Second opinions & health checks

🏆 In Return for Your Hard Work

  • A competitive compensation package (base + stock options), with half-year and annual performance reviews

  • The chance to work on patient-first, system-level healthcare challenges in one of Europe’s leading healthtech companies

  • Opportunities for growth and leadership we want you to challenge the status quo, own your impact, and continue developing, with our full support

🤝 Diversity at Doccla

We embrace diversity. To build a great product, we need a team with a wide range of perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences.

We’re committed to equal opportunity hiring regardless of race, religion, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, or background. If you're excited about the role, we encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't match every point.

🔐 Safer Recruitment

We are committed to safer recruitment practices. As Doccla is a CQC registered company, a Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check will be required for all roles.

It is an offence to apply for such work if you are barred from working with children or vulnerable adults.

🧑‍⚕️ What You’ll Do as a RA/QA Specialist

This role provides a RAQA Specialist for our Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) portfolio, based in the UK and supporting regulatory activities across the UK, EU, and international markets. The position is needed to maintain delivery continuity during an active notified body Technical Documentation and general QA support.

✅ What Experience You’ll Bring to the Team

SaMD Technical Documentation (Core Responsibility)
•Prepare, maintain, and update Technical Documentation in line with EU MDR and UK MDR 2002.
•Maintain the GSPR checklist, current objective evidence from SDLC, cybersecurity, usability, and risk management outputs.
•Own labelling and IFU compliance for software, including UDI, eIFU, in-app labelling, and UKCA/CE marking requirements.
•Support software qualification and classification rationale and intended purpose statements.
•Support clinical evaluation for software.
•Assess software releases and design changes for regulatory impact, including significant change determination and notified body notification.

Risk Management and Post-Market Surveillance
•Own and maintain the risk management file in line with ISO 14971 and ISO/TR 24971, including hazard analysis, risk controls, and benefit-risk determination for software.
•Support risk outputs are traceable to software requirements, verification, usability, and the Technical Documentation.
•Support PMS plan, PMS report / PSUR, and PMCF plan and evaluation report in line with EU MDR Articles 83 to 86 and Annex XIV Part B.
•Analyse complaints, incidents, trends, and real-world performance data, feeding outputs back into risk management and clinical evaluation.
•Support vigilance reporting to MHRA and EU competent authorities, including FSCAs and trend reporting.
•Act as a day-to-day point of contact for queries and commitments
•Coordinate with Engineering, Clinical, and Quality to ensure corrective actions are implemented and submission-ready.

UK and International Regulatory Strategy
•Support UKCA and CE marking, MHRA registrations
•Support international market access, including FDA (510(k)/De Novo) and other markets as the business expands.
•Monitor regulatory intelligence for SaMD and AI/ML (MHRA Software and AI as a Medical Device programme, MDCG guidance, FDA guidance, IMDRF) and assess impact on products and the QMS.
•Support CAPA and internal audit follow-ups where regulatory root causes are identified.

💡 What We’re Looking For

•3 to 6 years' Regulatory Affairs experience in Medical Devices, with a focus on SaMD.
Must-Have

  • EU MDR / UK MDR Technical Documentation for software: Proven experience preparing and maintaining it for notified body review.

  • ISO 14971: Hands-on experience owning a risk management file for SaMD.

  • SaMD qualification and classification: Practical application of MDCG 2019-11 / EU MDR Rule 11.

  • IEC 62304, IEC 82304-1, and IEC 62366-1 experience.

Good to have

  • Notified body interaction: Hands-on experience responding to NCs or review questions.

  • FDA submissions experience for software devices preferable

  • Experience with PMS plans, PSURs, and PMCF plans and reports.

item.title: Werkstudent:in (m/w/d) im Bereich Operations – Digital Health / Telemonitoring
item.description:
🌍 Über uns
Wir sind Doccla. Gemeinsam mit medizinischen Einrichtungen machen wir die Patientenversorgung unabhängig vom Ort und gestalten so mit, wie Menschen künftig versorgt werden.

Kern unseres Angebots ist eine eigene Telemonitoring-Software, mit der medizinisches Fachpersonal Patient:innen kontinuierlich aus der Ferne betreuen kann. Über unsere App übermitteln Patient:innen ihre Gesundheitsdaten direkt an das Behandlungsteam. Dazu stellen wir die erforderlichen Medizinprodukte bereit, übernehmen die Gerätelogistik und bieten telefonischen Support für Patient:innen und medizinisches Personal.

Wir arbeiten mit über 60 Prozent der regionalen Versorgungsverbünde im britischen NHS und sind in Irland, Frankreich und der DACH-Region aktiv. Finanziert durch eine Series B über 41 Mio. Euro, angeführt von Lakestar.

Seit 2023 bauen wir von München aus das Geschäft in Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz auf. Du gestaltest mit, wie neue Konzepte für Hospital at Home, Virtual Ward und Telemonitoring hier in die Versorgung kommen.

🚀 Deine Rolle bei uns
Du arbeitest direkt mit dem Head of Operations DACH zusammen und unterstützt uns dabei, unsere Lösung in der DACH-Region weiter auszubauen. Deine Aufgaben verteilen sich auf drei Bereiche.

Projektunterstützung, ca. 50 %

  • Du begleitest die Einführung unserer Lösung bei medizinischen Einrichtungen (z.B. Krankenhäuser oder Pflegeeinrichtungen), von der Vorbereitung bis zum Go-Live.

  • Du unterstützt bei Schulungen, Workshops und Kundenterminen, digital und vor Ort.

  • Du erstellst und pflegst Dokumentation: SOPs, Prozessbeschreibungen, Schulungsunterlagen.

  • Du behältst offene Aufgaben im Blick und koordinierst Termine zwischen unseren Teams und den Kunden.

Patient Support, ca. 30 %

  • Du bist erste Anlaufstelle für Patient:innen und medizinische Teams bei Fragen zu Software, Geräten und Abläufen, telefonisch und per E-Mail.

  • Viele unserer Patient:innen sind älter und wenig technikaffin. Du erklärst geduldig, auch mehrfach, und arbeitest strukturiert durch, bis das Problem gelöst ist.

  • Medizinische Fragen bearbeitest du nicht selbst. Du erkennst sie und gibst sie nach klaren Vorgaben an das medizinische Team weiter.

Geräte- und Logistik-Support, ca. 20 %

  • Du bereitest Telemonitoring-Geräte vor, konfigurierst sie und organisierst Versand und Rückläufer.

🎁 Was wir dir bieten

  • Eine spannende Rolle in einem der innovativsten Health-Tech-Unternehmen Europas

  • Die Möglichkeit, früh Verantwortung zu übernehmen und aktiv am Wachstum in der DACH-Region mitzuwirken

  • Einblicke in operative Abläufe, Projektmanagement und digitale medizinische Versorgungsprozesse

  • Flexibles Arbeiten in einem internationalen Scale-up mit offener Teamkultur

  • Viel Raum, eigene Ideen einzubringen und dich persönlich weiterzuentwickeln

💡 Was du mitbringen solltest

  • Du studierst im Bereich Gesundheitswesen, BWL, IT oder einem verwandten Fach.

  • Du arbeitest zuverlässig, eigenständig und dokumentierst sorgfältig.

  • Technisches Verständnis und Freude am Lösen von Problemen gehören für dich dazu.

  • Du sprichst verhandlungssicher Deutsch (C2 oder vergleichbar) und hast gute Englischkenntnisse für die interne Zusammenarbeit und Dokumentation.

  • Du kannst in unserem Münchener Büro vor Ort arbeiten.

⭐ Von Vorteil

  • Du hattest bereits berufliche Berührungspunkte mit dem deutschen oder österreichischen Gesundheitssystem.

  • Du tust dich mit österreichischem Deutsch leicht. Viele unserer Patient:innen rufen aus Österreich an, und wer Jänner, Jause, Spital und die e-card kennt, hat es am Telefon einfacher.

📍 Rahmenbedingungen

  • Standort: München

  • Arbeitszeit: Teilzeit (Werkstudent), 20h /Woche

  • Start: ab 01.10.2026

  • Vergütung: 18 € pro Stunde

Neugierig geworden?
Dann bewirb dich jetzt und sei dabei, wenn wir die Zukunft des digitalen Gesundheitswesens gestalten!

🧠 Wie wir arbeiten
Bei Doccla übernimmt jede:r Verantwortung für die eigene Arbeit. Patientensicherheit und Behandlungsergebnisse stehen für uns an erster Stelle. In dieser Rolle arbeitest du mit sensiblen Gesundheitsdaten. Entsprechende Schulungen und eine Verschwiegenheitsverpflichtung gehören zum Onboarding. Wir arbeiten pragmatisch und ergebnisorientiert, sprechen Dinge offen an und geben uns gegenseitig Feedback, unabhängig von der Position. Das DACH-Team arbeitet hybrid, mit Büro in München. Für diese Rolle sind feste Präsenztage vorgesehen, weil Gerätevorbereitung und Patientenkontakt vor Ort stattfinden. Darüber hinaus arbeiten wir eng mit unseren Kolleg:innen in London und Dänemark zusammen.

🤝 Vielfalt bei Doccla
Vielfalt ist ein zentraler Wert bei Doccla. Um ein Produkt zu entwickeln, das geschätzt wird, braucht es ein Team, das unterschiedlichste Perspektiven, Erfahrungen und Hintergründe vereint. Daher achten wir aktiv darauf, Menschen mit verschiedenen Hintergründen, Ethnien, Religionen, Geschlechtsidentitäten, sexuellen Orientierungen, Altersgruppen und Fähigkeiten einzustellen.

🧑‍⚕️ What You’ll Do as a Partnership Lead

This role owns Doccla's full Virtual Care portfolio within the region. Virtual Care spans two products: Virtual Wards, our established revenue-generating core, and Proactive Care, our primary growth ambition. Your focus sits firmly on proactive care, moving NHS systems toward outcome-based, population-scale programmes for their highest-risk patients. Alongside that, you act as the senior escalation point and NHS executive relationship owner for our existing Virtual Ward footprint, the proven base that earns us the right to the proactive care conversation. These are not two jobs. They are one Virtual Care offer across the acuity spectrum, and your task is to convert the credibility of the core into transformational growth.

Strategic Growth & Market Leadership

  • Act as the Senior Deal Architect for regional strategic growth, working with our senior leadership team as "Deal Sponsors" to orchestrate high-stakes opportunities across Acute Trusts, Community Trusts, Integrated Care Boards (ICBs) and GP Federations.

  • Turn existing relationships into growth: Use our established Virtual Ward accounts as the entry point for proactive care conversations, expanding the depth and value of relationships we already hold rather than starting cold.

  • Navigate the "Political Economy" of the NHS: Map and influence the complex web of stakeholders (Clinical, Financial, and Operational) to build multi-threaded sponsorship that remains resilient through leadership churn and policy shifts.

  • Leverage the Doccla Ecosystem: High-level orchestration of our Strategic Advisors, Investors and Senior Leadership Team to create "top-to-top" alignment with NHS Board members.

Deal Construction & Value-Based Orchestration

  • Lead the "Value-Based" Narrative: Translate clinical outcomes into hard financial ROI. You will shape propositions where Doccla's success is intrinsically linked to system savings and patient throughput.

  • Drive Complex "Deal Sprints": Own the end-to-end lifecycle of large-scale tenders and direct awards, aligning internal Product, Clinical, and Finance teams to ensure each deal is not just "winnable" but operationally and financially viable over a multi-year horizon.

  • Master Commercial Complexity: Shape the logic behind pricing models, gain-share mechanisms, and procurement routes (e.g. Frameworks vs. Bespoke Tenders) to ensure commercial clarity in the face of deferred payment milestones.

Stakeholder Mobilisation & Clinical Credibility

  • C-Suite Relationship Management: Maintain "trusted advisor" status with senior executives, moving beyond a vendor relationship to a strategic partnership.

  • Senior Escalation Point for Virtual Wards: Act as the NHS executive relationship owner and escalation point for our existing Virtual Ward footprint, protecting that revenue, safeguarding renewals, and keeping these relationships strong enough to carry the proactive care conversation.

  • High-Stakes Content & Communication: Produce Board-level business cases and investment proposals that stand out for their clinical depth, commercial rigour, and simplicity.

  • Mobilisation Transition: Ensure a seamless "handover of intent" from contract signature to operational launch, embedding the value-based metrics agreed during the sale into the delivery roadmap.

✅ What Experience You’ll Bring to the Team

  • 5+ years experience in NHS facing commercial roles (healthtech, medtech, consulting, or services), with a track record of owning and closing complex opportunities.

  • Demonstrable experience navigating NHS structures and buying dynamics, including ICB and multi provider decision making, procurement, IG, and clinical governance.

  • Existing senior relationships in the NHS, ideally across Northern systems, with evidence you can open doors and create momentum quickly.

  • Strong comfort with quantitative work: building clear analysis, financial cases, outcomes framing, and pricing models that stand up to scrutiny.

  • Experience working cross functionally to deliver ambiguous, high pace workstreams, not just selling a fixed product.

  • High productivity mindset, including confident use of modern tools and automation to move faster and operate at scale.

💡 What We’re Looking For

  • A senior operator with integrity, energy, and a bias to action who can create clarity and pace in complex environments.

  • Exceptional communicator who can shift between board level narrative and detailed working sessions with clinical and operational teams.

  • Commercial judgement and negotiation strength: you can hold the line on value while building trust and long term partnerships.

  • Comfortable being accountable for outcomes, not activity, and able to lead without heavy oversight.

  • Excited by a fast growing startup environment where iteration, learning, and ownership are expected

🧠 How We Work

We empower everyone at Doccla to take ownership of their work and the company's mission. We act ethically and always put patient safety and outcomes first.

To thrive here, you’ll need a can-do attitude and an action-oriented approach, along with a willingness to learn and grow through open feedback.
